key_insight: A conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes formulation retains second-Brinkman effects through standard finite-volume central differencing, improving accuracy without separate discretisation.
engineering_relevance: DBS2 enables accurate digital-rock flow and permeability prediction directly on voxelized micro-CT images while preserving DBS1 computational efficiency.
method: Write the full DBS equation in conservative form.
Apply standard central differencing to retain the full viscous-stress terms.
Implement DBS2 in GeoChemFoam and compare against DNS benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across microchannel, 2D micromodel, and 3D Bentheimer sandstone benchmarks, DBS2 reproduced the microchannel DNS velocity field exactly and matched DNS permeability within 1.5–3.8% in the latter two cases; DBS1 overpredicted permeability by 14.1–37.9%.
watch_item: Validation covers three benchmarks at matched spatial resolution; accuracy across broader rock geometries and coarser voxel resolutions remains unestablished.
paper_title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for Digital Rock Flow Simulation with Embedded Second-Brinkman Effects
